headline: Preprint reports predictable failures in rarity- and relevance-based memory for LLM group decisions
summary: The arXiv preprint introduces CrossProfile, a diagnostic with 60 main templates and 480 ownership variants that keeps fact wording fixed while varying which agents hold supporting, decoy and irrelevant information. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and exploratory hosted DeepSeek runs, the authors report that rarity-first and relevance-first memory heuristics can reverse performance depending on who holds decoy evidence. In the classic hidden-profile condition, relevance-first selection lowers accuracy by about 20–22 points for the two local models, and removing or randomizing holder-attribution tags raises accuracy by about 13–14 points. The study uses constructed tasks and a mechanically defined answer key; it does not estimate failure rates in deployed teams.
